title: The Long Defence
author: a gate-warden
pages: We held the ford three nights. I write down the order of it so I do not forget it, though I would like to.

They came first as men and orcs, and those we could have held. Then the dark came up out of the ground the way fire does, only black. Each time it flared there were more of them standing in it, and none of those were living.
He stood at the back of them and did not come closer. He did not need to.
Five stood with us. The old one with the beard, who made it day for the space of a breath. The woman whose wall they could not cross. The swordsman. The big one in plate, who burned them.
The fifth I cannot describe. I have tried. He was there, and when it was over the one at the back had gone down into the ground, and the dark with him.
My grandmother says the four are still about, in a way. She says the fifth is too, though he never had much to say. I do not ask her what she means.
